httpExemption: Notifications' worker has no HTTP surface at all: the service's one, the BFF's gRPC hop (§3.2), is notifications-api's and judged under that descriptor (ADR-118). This chart renders no Service, no route reaches it, and its only listener is §13.5's health endpoint, which the http templates exclude by route. A declared http signal would read a series that is empty by construction, and an empty result rolls every rung back, so the rollout could only ever fail. The events it subscribes to (§3.2) arrive on the broker and are judged by consume. The send and push workers are where this service's risk sits and neither is a consumer, so the contact read, the relay and the push providers carry no canary signal of their own — notifications.waiting, notifications.mail.unavailable, notifications.push.unavailable, notifications.push.refused and notifications.contact.refused are what watch them, outside the rollout, and docs/runbooks/queue-backlog.md says what neither sees.
